questions.stimulus: A made-up village. A teacher finds two old sources. A photo shows a small school with about 20 children. A letter says, "Our new school opened this year."
questions.question: What can you say by using both sources?

options.text: The village had a new school with about 20 children.
Every child in the village loved going to school.
The school is still open today.

questions.stimulus: An old shop receipt says: "Rice, 12 coins."
questions.question: Which question needs a different source to answer it?

options.text: How much did the rice cost?
What did this shop sell?
How did people feel on market day?

questions.stimulus: An old cup has a crack. Someone glued the crack.
questions.question: Which sentence is an observation?

options.text: The owner of the cup was poor.
The cup has a crack that was glued.
The cup was a gift from a friend.

questions.stimulus: Historian A reads one family's letters from one week. Historian B looks at maps of a whole country over 200 years.
questions.question: What is the main difference between their work?

options.text: Only Historian A uses sources.
They study the past at different scales: close and wide.
Historian B learns more about one family's feelings.

questions.stimulus: A museum has an old bag. Nobody is sure who owned it.
questions.question: Which museum label is the most careful?

options.text: This bag may have belonged to a teacher.
This bag belonged to a famous teacher.
Nobody can learn anything from this bag.

questions.question: Which part of a map tells you what each symbol means?

options.text: The title
The compass rose
The key

questions.stimulus: A made-up map. The footpath from the school to the market is 300 metres. The road is 900 metres. It rained all night.
questions.question: What do you still need to find out before you choose a route?

options.text: Which route is shorter on the map.
Whether the footpath is muddy or safe after the rain.
Where the market is on the map.
This town is usually hot and wet for half of every year.
It is raining hard this afternoon.
It was windy yesterday morning.

questions.stimulus: A made-up town. A new railway station opens. Factories open near the station, and they need workers.
questions.question: What will probably happen next?

options.text: The town gets smaller.
More people move to the town for jobs.
The factories close at once.

questions.question: A city grows very fast. Which problem is most likely?

options.text: Schools and clinics become crowded.
Fewer people ride the buses.
Nobody needs new homes.

questions.stimulus: Dina speaks Arabic, English and some Indonesian. At a clinic, she helps a new family talk to the nurse.
questions.question: What does this show?

options.text: Families should not go to clinics alone.
It is best to speak only one language.
Speaking more than one language is a useful skill.

questions.stimulus: Kofi gives Sara some bread. Sara gives Kofi some eggs. They use no money.
questions.question: What is this kind of exchange called?

options.text: Saving
Borrowing
Barter

questions.stimulus: A notice at a centre has words and also small pictures: food, a clock and a calendar.
questions.question: Why are the pictures helpful?

options.text: More people can understand the notice, even if they read little of the language.
The pictures make the notice longer.
Only children can understand pictures.

questions.stimulus: A message says: "SHARE NOW!! The water at the centre will be unsafe tomorrow!!" It has no name, no date and no link.
questions.question: What is the best thing to do first?

options.text: Share it quickly with everyone you know.
Check who made it, when, and what the evidence is.
Believe it, because it uses capital letters.

questions.stimulus: A post says, "The road is flooded today." Its photo is real, but it was taken three years ago.
questions.question: What is the problem with this post?

options.text: Photos are always fake.
The road was never flooded.
The photo is old, so it cannot show the road today.

questions.stimulus: Mei has 10 coins. She can buy a snack now, or save the coins for a book next week.
questions.question: What do we call a choice where you give up one thing to get another?

options.text: A rumour
A trade-off
A barrier

writing.title: A made-up town
clues: Clue 1: A photo from last year shows a new bridge over the river.
Clue 2: A shop owner's notebook says that this year, many more customers came from the other side of the river.
writing.prompt: What do you think happened in this town? Write 2 or 3 sentences. Use one clue to support your idea.

confidence: I can explain what a source tells us.
I can use a map to find information.
I can give a reason for my answer.
I can share my ideas with a partner.
I can tell if information might not be true.

rubric.zero: No idea about what happened, or an idea the clues don't touch.
rubric.one: An idea about what happened, but unclear.
rubric.two: A clear idea about what happened (for example, the bridge brought more customers to the shop).

rubric.one: A clue mentioned, but not exactly ("the photo").
rubric.two: A detail from a clue used exactly (the new bridge, or more customers from the other side).

rubric.zero: No link between the clue and the idea.
rubric.one: A link that is only implied.
rubric.two: Explains how the clue supports the idea, or names a limit (for example, the notebook is from one shop only).
